NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Site Reliability / Platform Engineer
Manchester, UK | nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior SRE and platform engineer with 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six years operating Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Experienced in cloud infrastructure engineering, AWS environment design and operation, Terraform, platform architecture, and building reliable, observable platforms for product teams. Tech lead for a five-person platform team, with a track record of leading technical initiatives and agreeing reliability approaches with product leadership.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), Linux
Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Atlantis
Kubernetes and platforms: Kubernetes, Helm, Kustomize, Argo CD, Crossplane, Karpenter
Reliability and observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs and error budgets, incident management
Programming and automation: Go, Python, Bash, GitHub Actions, Puppet
Testing and capacity planning: k6

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS)
Manchester / remote | Apr 2022 – present
- Tech lead of a five-person platform team operating an AWS EKS platform across eight clusters and three regions, supporting approximately 350 services.
- Built an internal developer platform with Go and Python service templates, Argo CD GitOps, and Crossplane self-service for RDS, SQS and S3. Adopted by all 14 product teams; reduced the time to take a new service to production from approximately two weeks to under one day.
- Introduced SLOs, burn-rate alerts and error budgets for the 20 most critical services, agreeing the error budget policy with product leadership. Reduced on-call pages per week by approximately 60%.
- Led migration from cluster-autoscaler managed node groups to Karpenter, using Spot instances for stateless workloads with interruption handling. Reduced EC2 spend by 38% (approximately £410,000 per year).
- Participate in the incident commander rotation and established the incident and post-mortem process.
- Mentored three engineers transitioning from backend development into SRE.

Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games
Leeds | Jan 2019 – Mar 2022
- Operated AWS game backend infrastructure using EC2, ECS and later EKS for titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players.
- Managed AWS infrastructure in Terraform (approximately 40 modules), using Atlantis for plan and apply workflows on pull requests.
- Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability stack.
- Led load testing and launch-day capacity planning. Used k6 to simulate 300,000 concurrent players and identified a connection pool limit before launch.

Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting
Sheffield | Jul 2016 – Dec 2018
- Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet for configuration management.
- Automated operational tasks with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer incidents.

SELECTED PROJECT
Kubernetes preview namespace cleanup operator | Open source, 2024
- Built a small Kubernetes controller in Go using controller-runtime to delete expired preview namespaces; the project has approximately 120 GitHub stars.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016

CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021; renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional | 2023

SELECTED SPEAKING
“SLOs that product managers care about” | UK DevOps meetup | 2024

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Urdu (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with a clear senior SRE/platform-engineering profile. It uses quantified outcomes effectively: adoption by all 14 product teams, production lead-time reduction, 60% fewer pages, 38% lower EC2 spend, support for 350 services, and platforms serving 1.2 million daily players. The experience section demonstrates progression, technical leadership, reliability ownership, observability, cost optimization, and mentoring. The document is professional and substantially more complete than a typical technical CV. The main content limitation is that some role-relevant areas—particularly networking security protocols and system-design terminology—are not evidenced, but these are candidate-experience gaps rather than writing defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard section headings, conventional chronology, text-based formatting, clear job titles, recognizable technology names, and measurable results. It should parse reliably and has a high AI-screening probability for AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, platform engineering, SRE, observability, incident management, and technical leadership searches. Matching is likely to be weaker for exact searches involving Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, IoT, JVM, and virtual machines because those terms are not supported by the candidate information and should not be added. The skills section is readable and well categorized; the only useful ATS enhancement is to use a few of the job advertisement's supported phrases more explicitly in the summary and experience bullets.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns very well with the hands-on infrastructure, AWS, cloud operation, Terraform, platform architecture, reliability, observability, and technical-leadership aspects of the role. The strongest evidence includes operating multi-region EKS, designing an internal developer platform, managing AWS infrastructure with Terraform, leading capacity planning, establishing SLO and incident processes, and agreeing an error-budget policy with product leadership. It also shows analytical thinking and communication through measurable reliability improvements, launch testing, stakeholder alignment, mentoring, and the SLO presentation. Candidate-material gaps for this specific role are strong Terragrunt experience, mTLS/SSL/TLS and certificate-management experience, explicit IoT or remote-device integration, JVM experience, and explicit virtual-machine experience. The document does show Linux and AWS EC2 experience, but not a distinct virtual-machine focus. These gaps should not be treated as CV defects or addressed by adding unsupported claims.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENT 1 — In the Professional Summary, change "Experienced in cloud infrastructure engineering, AWS environment design and operation, Terraform, platform architecture" to "Experienced in hands-on infrastructure engineering, AWS cloud environment design and operation, Terraform, and platform architecture." This uses the advert's wording more directly while remaining fully supported by the candidate's experience.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT 2 — In the Brightwater Games experience section, change "Managed AWS infrastructure in Terraform (approximately 40 modules), using Atlantis for plan and apply workflows on pull requests" to "Managed all AWS infrastructure in Terraform across approximately 40 modules, using Atlantis for plan and apply workflows on pull requests." This more clearly communicates the breadth of the candidate's infrastructure ownership and strengthens the exact Terraform keyword match.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from infrastructure engineering to senior platform leadership. The strongest content is quantified and outcome-focused: adoption by all 14 product teams, production lead time reduced from two weeks to under one day, 60% fewer on-call pages, and 38% lower EC2 spend. The document also communicates technical leadership without overstating people-management responsibilities. The main content limitation is that several relevant areas from the candidate material are either underrepresented or absent, particularly the Linux Systems Engineer experience, the detailed systems architecture context behind the internal developer platform, and the candidate's concrete capacity-planning and stakeholder-facing work. Removing the Pennine Hosting role was explicitly requested, so its absence is not treated as an error.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly standard headings, conventional reverse-chronological structure, searchable technology names, and readable bullet formatting. It should parse well and has a high AI-screening probability because it combines role-relevant keywords with specific scale and impact metrics. Alignment could be improved by explicitly using supported job-ad language such as "cloud environment design and operation," "systems architecture," "system design," "technical proposals," and "stakeholder alignment." Terraform is clearly present, but Terragrunt is not present and should not be added because it is not supported by the candidate information. The current skills section is comprehensive without relying on unsupported technologies such as Istio, Linkerd, or full Backstage ownership.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV is a strong match for hands-on AWS infrastructure engineering, cloud platform operation, Terraform, Kubernetes, observability, reliability, technical leadership, and stakeholder alignment. The internal developer platform, self-service infrastructure, SLO programme, incident processes, and capacity-planning work fit Corvale's engineering-led, ownership-oriented environment well. The candidate also demonstrates Linux experience and backend-infrastructure exposure through game platforms, although not JVM development. The principal requirement gaps are Terragrunt, mTLS/SSL/TLS and certificate management, and IoT, automotive, or remote-device integration; the candidate information does not establish experience in those areas. Practical security awareness is also not explicitly evidenced. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that can be solved by rewriting. The CV can, however, make the candidate's existing architecture, networking-adjacent AWS, analytical, and stakeholder work more visible.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the current second sentence with wording that uses the advert's supported terminology more directly: "Experienced in hands-on infrastructure engineering, AWS cloud environment design and operation, Terraform, platform architecture, and building reliable, observable platforms for product teams." Retain the existing sentence about leading a five-person platform team and agreeing reliability approaches with product leadership.
2. In the Senior Platform Engineer section under Tallybrook Ltd, revise the internal developer platform bullet to make the systems-architecture and technical-proposal scope explicit without adding unsupported claims. For example: "Designed and built an internal developer platform using Go and Python service templates, Argo CD GitOps, and Crossplane self-service for RDS, SQS and S3; led the technical approach from implementation through adoption by all 14 product teams, reducing time to production from approximately two weeks to under one day." 
3. In the same Tallybrook section, revise the SLO bullet to foreground stakeholder alignment: "Introduced SLOs, burn-rate alerts and error budgets for the 20 most critical services; agreed the error-budget policy with product leadership and reduced on-call pages per week by approximately 60%." This is already substantially present, but the revised wording places the job's stakeholder requirement in a more searchable position.
4. In the Brightwater Games section, expand the load-testing bullet using the supported evidence from the candidate portfolio: "Led analytical load testing and launch-day capacity planning; used k6 to simulate 300,000 concurrent players and identified a connection-pool limit before launch." This gives stronger evidence for analytical thinking and systems performance assessment.
5. In the Core Skills section, change the heading "Cloud infrastructure" to "Cloud infrastructure and environment operation" and retain the existing AWS and Linux technologies underneath it. This improves keyword alignment while staying truthful.
6. In the Core Skills section, retain Terraform and Atlantis but do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, IoT, automotive, or other unsupported technologies. The absence of those terms is an experience gap, not a document defect that should be filled speculatively.
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- “Led load testing”

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, concise, professional, and strongly evidence-based. It presents senior-level platform and SRE experience through measurable outcomes: 350 services across eight clusters, adoption by 14 product teams, a 60% reduction in on-call pages, and a 38% reduction in EC2 spend. The experience section is particularly persuasive for infrastructure, Kubernetes, AWS, reliability, and technical leadership. The main content weakness is not writing quality but role-specific coverage: the CV does not demonstrate networking/security topics requested by the employer, and it does not explicitly describe systems architecture or stakeholder-facing technical proposals in the employer's terminology. The omission of the earlier Linux Systems Engineer role is consistent with the user's instruction, and Linux remains represented in the skills section.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses standard headings, simple paragraphs, conventional bullet points, clear job titles, dates, and recognizable technology names, so it should parse well in most ATS and AI screening systems. The HTML structure is generally ATS-friendly, although a plain-text or standard DOCX/PDF export should be checked to ensure bullets, dates, contact details, and section headings remain correctly extractable. Alignment would improve if supported terms such as "systems architecture," "system design," "technical proposals," "stakeholder management," and "network design" were used explicitly. Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, or security technologies because they are not supported by the candidate information. AI screening probability is high for AWS/Kubernetes/platform/SRE roles, but moderate rather than high for this specific vacancy because several stated must-haves are absent or not evidenced.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV is a strong match for hands-on infrastructure engineering, AWS cloud operation, Terraform, Kubernetes platforms, observability, reliability, technical leadership, and analytical problem-solving. The internal developer platform work is particularly relevant to helping backend developers deploy services that are easy to monitor and run. The candidate also demonstrates stakeholder alignment through agreeing the error-budget policy with product leadership and achieving adoption by all 14 product teams. The candidate's material does not show Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS, practical security work, IoT/automotive/remote-device integration, JVM development, or virtual-machine experience; these are genuine profile gaps rather than CV-writing defects. AWS, Linux, and backend-infrastructure exposure are shown. No direct fleet, train, or remote-device integration experience is evidenced.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the generic phrase "platform architecture" with a more evidence-based and job-aligned statement that reflects the documented work: "Experienced in hands-on infrastructure engineering, AWS cloud environment operation, Terraform-based infrastructure, internal platform architecture, and building reliable, observable platforms for product teams." This avoids overstating unsupported breadth while making the ad's terminology easier for ATS screening to detect.

2. In the Senior Platform Engineer experience entry at Tallybrook Ltd, revise the internal developer platform bullet to explicitly show systems design and technical leadership. For example: "Designed the internal developer platform architecture and led the technical approach from implementation through adoption by all 14 product teams, using Go and Python service templates, Argo CD GitOps, and Crossplane self-service for RDS, SQS, and S3; reduced time to production from approximately two weeks to under one day." This is supported by the candidate portfolio and better matches the employer's requirements for system design and leading technical proposals.

3. In the Senior Platform Engineer experience section, change "Participate in the incident commander rotation and established the incident and post-mortem process" to "Participate in the incident commander rotation and established the incident-management and post-mortem process." This corrects the tense inconsistency and makes the operational ownership clearer.

4. In the Professional Summary or the Tallybrook experience section, explicitly connect the documented product-leadership work to stakeholder alignment. Add a truthful sentence or bullet such as: "Agreed reliability and error-budget policy with product leadership and drove adoption of the platform across all 14 product teams." This is supported by the existing CV and candidate portfolio and directly addresses bringing stakeholders along.

MINOR ATS ENHANCEMENT:
5. In the Core Skills section, change the label "Cloud infrastructure and environment operation" to "Cloud infrastructure engineering and environment design and operation" only if the detailed Tallybrook and Brightwater bullets remain immediately below it. This uses the job's terminology while remaining supported by the documented AWS platform and infrastructure work.

Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, IoT, JVM, virtual machines, or security tools to the CV: the original candidate information does not substantiate those technologies or experiences.
